recipes.name: Edamame, Corn, and Black Bean Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 pound) package frozen shelled edamame (green soybeans)
1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Make the vinaigrette: Whisk cilantro, vinegar, oil, lime juice, garlic, sugar, and salt together in a large bowl until well combined.
Make the salad: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add edamame and cook for 3 minutes. Add corn and cook for 1 more minute. Drain very well.

Pour edamame and corn into the large bowl with vinaigrette, then add beans, cherry tomatoes, and green onions; gently mix until all ingredients are coated. Cover and refrigerate until flavors have blended, at least 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Edamame, Corn, and Black Bean Salad
raw_recipe.description: This edamame, corn, and black bean salad tossed in a cilantro-lime vinaigrette is a nice alternative to a green garden salad.

video.description: This simple and colorful salad features black beans, corn, cherry tomatoes, and edamame, dressed up with a light and lively lime vinaigrette dressing.

review.reviewBody: Loved this salad! I also used olive oil in place of the grapeseed. Wonderful summertime salad that would work well for a pot-luck. Sylvia thank you for sharing. The average lime yields 2T/1oz juice.

TRUE five-star Winner! Vegetarian cooking at its best. The boring title belies its great taste =) Great mix of colors, flavors, and textures. If the dressing seems too tangy, I would lessen the vinegar, NOT the lime. I used EV olive oil and cut up 3 large regular tomatoes (which I seeded first). I mixed the corn and soybeans with the dressing first, than tasted a spoonful with every subsequent addition...every bite was great--you could leave out something and still have a great salad. Canned corn also works in a pinch with only a slightly less "crunchy" result. I have served this over salad greens alongside hot cornbread, and also with rice. My new favorite recipe!!!! =)

LOVE this salad! The first time I made it was for a 4th of July picnic, and my family devoured it. I have used fresh sweet corn when in season, but frozen is just as good the rest of the year. I do make a few changes to the recipe. I highly recommend roasting the corn first as it really brings out the sweetness. I spread the corn on a baking sheet, toss with just enough olive oil to coat and roast it in the oven at 400 for 15-20 min (less if using fresh), stirring halfway through and watching carefully so it doesn’t get too charred. My other changes are just based on personal preferences - I use a small red onion instead of the green onions, and I use only half the amount of black beans. The vinaigrette I make as written but salt to taste, which is usually a bit less than called for (at first I tried cutting back the amount of sugar as well, but it definitely needs it!). This is a great recipe that can be easily adapted to individual tastes.

This is SO GOOD! I decreased the corn to 1-1/2 cups and added 1/2 of an orange pepper and half of a yellow pepper chopped up instead. I also didn't have grapeseed oil so I just used canola oil. The dressing is delightful. Truly a light, healthy, delicious salad!

You can't mess this up! Just made it and don't know if I can wait 2 hours to eat it! Used white wine vinegar (out of red), olive oil, garbanzo beans (no edamame in the house), and didn't cook the frozen corn - so NO cooking on this very hot day! Think the lime juice makes it. But honestly all kinds of substitutions from vinegar to oil to beans probably will work. Going to serve it over lettuce with avocado slices on the side. Add baguette rounds toasted with olive oil and salt and pepper and dinner is served!

I thought this was so light and delicous! I made several changes, I used cranberry pear balsamic vinegar as I did not have the red wine vinegar. I used roasted red pepper in place of tomatoes because we are fans of peppers. I used olive oil instead of grape seed. I used garbanzo instead of black beans ( again personal pref) and red onion instead of green. I used fresh corn on the cob that I blanched. 4 ears made exactly 3 cups. This will be my go to recipe for taking to friends BBQ's. I rarely give 5 stars but this deserved it. It is better if made the night before.

Made this before a cook-out for some friends. It was incredibly well received and everyone loved it! I added Avocados and used red bell pepper instead of tomatoes. It's flavorful, easy to prepare and REALLY good for you! This is a WIN! 

Oh! And a good tip is to put the dressing on the edamame and corn when it's HOT. The beans just drink up the flavor!

I love the dressing! I had to use one lemon and one lime, but it was nice and tangy, salty and sweet. This is the first time I've tried edamame, its ok - the salad is nice and refreshing, healthy and so colorful! I didnt boil the corn, you can just throw it in the bowl frozen.

This recipe is a keeper! I just used it as inspiration as I did not have all the ingredients on hand and wanted something fresh tasting to put into some flour tortillas. My filler was as follows: can of black beans, can of corn, 4 green onions, 2 cloves garlic, cut up ripe mango, 3/4 kosher salt, 1 tsp. white sugar, juice of 1/2 lemon, 3 tbs. red wine vinegar, 2 tbs. peanut oil. Wow, was it ever good. I just had two tortillas filled with this mix and am ready to make myself one more for lunch. I would feel like a glutton, but not too bad since this is so much more of a healthy option. I can't wait to make the whole salad as directed. This also made plenty of salad for 2-3 days worth of lunch tortillas.
Cook the edamame for 1 minute and then cook the corn for 1 minute. I also added pepper to the final salad and more salt.

I have made this three times. The first time exactly per the instructions. The 2nd and third times dropped back on the amount of corn by half, finely diced 2 stalks of celery and 2 carrots and added a more cilantro. The carrots and celery add some additional color and crunch. Served it as a side to sandwiches at lunch or as a side to chicken or pork for dinner. Keeps very well for a few days in the fridge.

I hosted a neighborhood party and this was a great hit, healthy and colorful alongside the macaroni and cheese and meatballs. Several people asked for the recipe; my husband is eating the leftovers and asking me to make it again. I, too, used olive oil as that is what I had, and I doubled the dressing and then served it with a slotted spoon so the dressing could drain off if necessary.

I made it a day ahead and cheated by using Red Wine Vinaigrette dressing to use up the bottle, but the next time I make it it will be from the recipe. A couple sliced radishes were added for crunch. This is a great salad and so different. Thank you so much for sharing it.
This salad was amazing!! And super easy to make, me and my fiancé loved it!!
very nice recipes short and sweet. Easy to understand . You made the servings to adjust.thats so nice.but make it in grams.
This was delicious exactly as written. It's even better as a left over. The whole family loved it!
